gloss: how something looks on screen or in photos; image quality

definitions.gloss: how something looks on screen or in photos; image quality
definitions.explanation: The way something appears when photographed, filmed, or reflected.

definitions.gloss: how well things go together; harmony of appearance
definitions.explanation: The way colors, patterns, or items complement each other visually.

examples.japanese: テレビの{映|うつ}りが{悪|わる}い。
examples.english: The picture quality on the TV is bad.

examples.japanese: この{写真|しゃしん}は{映|うつ}りがいいね。
examples.english: You look good in this photo.

examples.japanese: {鏡|かがみ}の{映|うつ}りを{確認|かくにん}してから{出|で}かけた。
examples.english: I checked my reflection in the mirror before heading out.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}と{白|しろ}は{映|うつ}りがいい。
examples.english: Red and white look good together.

examples.japanese: {着物|きもの}と{帯|おび}の{映|うつ}りを{考|かんが}える。
examples.english: Think about how the kimono and obi look together.

examples.japanese: {壁|かべ}の{色|いろ}との{映|うつ}りを{気|き}にして{家具|かぐ}を{選|えら}んだ。
examples.english: I chose the furniture considering how it would look against the wall color.

notes:
The noun form of {映|うつ}る (to be reflected, to appear on screen). Describes how something looks when reflected, photographed, or displayed.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {映|うつ}りがいい: looks good (on screen/in photos), photogenic
- {映|うつ}りが{悪|わる}い: looks bad (on screen/in photos)
- テレビの{映|うつ}り: TV picture quality
- {写真|しゃしん}の{映|うつ}り: how one looks in photos

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {写|うつ}り: how something looks in a photograph — written with a different kanji but pronounced the same; the two are often used interchangeably for photos
- {見栄|みば}え: visual appeal, appearance — focuses on how attractive something looks overall

USAGE:
{映|うつ}りがいい is commonly used to compliment someone who looks good in photos. This is different from the person being attractive in general — it specifically refers to how well the camera captures them.

cross_references.label: written with 写 for photos specifically
